checks.detail: The detached Ed25519 JWS verifies under the caller-trusted receipt-issuer key.
Only an administrator-configured relationship was observed; interactive human authorization was not proven.
The verified action credential and receipt name the same agent identity.
The agent proved possession of the key bound by the receipt and credential.
The signed action credential carries the exact signed-receipt digest.
Receipt and credential address the exercised payments gate.
Preview was safely denied because the required human witness was absent.
A newly signed but differently digested receipt could not be paired with the existing credential.
An unavailable revocation answer remained visibly indeterminate and produced no effect.
A signed administrator-configured label did not satisfy an interactive-consent policy.
The receipt was valid before its receipt-specific handle was revoked.
The next preview attempt was rejected after receipt revocation.
Provider witness references, receipt ID, credential ID, and gate outcomes form one reconstructable path.

limitations: The current ZITADEL fixture proves an administrator-authored link and role grant, not an interactive human authorization event.
The receipt issuer and short-lived action credential authority are benchmark-owned neutral components, not provider-native features.
Provider bearer tokens, JWS values, signatures, private keys, and raw proofs are not retained.
